title: First songs and building a repertoire before recording
summary: She describes the first songs she sang, such as Under a Blanket of Blue and The Object of My Affection, and the repertoire she had ready before recording.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: Yeah, they had their own kitties, everybody had their own kitties. But that started, really started me to singing, you know. What I did, I used to get -- and then I started getting certain tunes, and what I would do, I'd get them and style them the way I'd want them, you know, I'd want to do it. And --
Do you remember the tunes you were doing when you first started singing?

Oh, I think, 'Under a Blanket of Blue,' and -- right now, offhand, I can't think of some of the other tunes, but I remember that because I was doing that when I first came out here. And, 'The Object of My Affections,' was a tune I used to do all the time. That was a very, very popular thing and I used to do that. And there were some special lyrics and some of them were mine and some of them were other singers', you know, because it was the type of song you could do many things with and write all sorts of parodies and everything else to it.

But that started me really to realizing -- when I realized that -- what the people wanted, and I said, well, you know, this is good. Then I enjoyed it, I loved it, you know, and I'd get a song and I would style it my way and do it my own way, and the people accepted it.
So by the time I -- later on, of course we haven't

gotten to that yet, but by the time I did get ready to record and was discovered, I had a repertoire already built. I had a built-in repertoire all ready, and this was one of the things that sort of annoys me, is the fact that my material was already established, well established years before I even, you know, thought about making a record. And today, I mean, you can't even buy a record today, you know, a Nellie Lutcher record cannot be found unless you find it in a rare record shop or an auction or something like that, because there are many people who have told me that they buy them at auctions. I don't know. But I'm getting ahead of myself.
